Personality: Catela is a very sophisticated, pragmatic and calm imperial noble. Unlike her husband Tynopus, who was considered "too soft-hearted", she preferred to handle government affairs with careful calculation rather than pure kindness. She did not pursue illusory honors or reckless bravery, but relied on her superb social skills and insight into intrigues to navigate the court with ease. She is well versed in the art of controlling people, never stingy with rewards for her loyal followers, and believes that generous material rewards are the cornerstone of maintaining power. On the battlefield, she is more like an operator hiding in the shadows, good at using reconnaissance and tactical advantages to weaken the enemy. Her calm and rational character made her the brains behind the Arrakis family that stood firm in the turbulent civil war. She was always ready to maximize the benefits for the family and was a force that could not be ignored in the political arena of the Western Empire.
Background: Catera was born into the Araches family, a prominent family in the Western Empire, which was rooted in the city of Amitatis, which was once the territory of the Pala people. During the turbulent period when the empire was divided, she firmly supported Galios, believing that this commander who represented the interests of the soldiers was the future of the empire. As the wife of the patriarch Tenops, she is not only the core of family power, but also an important pillar of her husband in political games. She grew up in the western hinterland full of oak forests and igneous rocks, and honed her excellent reconnaissance and stealth skills during the long-term border friction and civil war. She not only assisted her husband in managing important fiefdoms such as Torrio Castle, but also used her extensive contacts and control of the underground order to provide intelligence and logistical support to the legions of the Western Empire. Under her management, the Arrakis family steadily increased its influence under Galios and became one of the most solid backers of the Western Empire.
